papers.title: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
papers.brief: DyCraft让编码智能体先规划并搭建静态场景，再生成可独立调试的关键姿态分镜；以验证后的起止状态为边界，调用运动创作工具完成局部动画。
papers.tldr: 将长时程动画拆成可独立验证的三维分镜与局部运动，减少物理错误。
papers.what_it_is: DyCraft让编码智能体先规划并搭建静态场景，再生成可独立调试的关键姿态分镜；以验证后的起止状态为边界，调用运动创作工具完成局部动画。
key_points: 三维分镜将关键姿态转为可独立调试的静态场景
运动创作工具连接已验证的起止状态
24项长时程多镜头任务中，物理违规更少
papers.why_notable: 把一次性动画脚本改为可验证的分段创作，缓解复杂时空约束的纠错难题；相比原生编码智能体及既有基线，人类评价更偏好其结果。
papers.abstract: While frontier coding agents can generate high-quality 3D scenes and articulated assets, they struggle to create coherent long-horizon animations. When equipped with general-purpose harnesses, they frequently produce physically implausible outputs, generating objects that interpenetrate, lack physical support, or move unnaturally. Such bare agents struggle to repair these errors because they default to scripting the full animation in one pass, making it difficult to verify their work and disentangle complex spatiotemporal constraints. Drawing on the practice of human animators, we introduce DyCraft, a system for animated 3D scene generation that breaks animation into steps that coding agents can more reliably solve. DyCraft first expands the user's prompt into a detailed plan and builds a static scene. It then creates a 3D storyboard of key animation poses, where each frame is a static 3D scene that the agent can build and debug in isolation. Storyboarding decomposes the problem into pairs of verified start and end states, allowing the agent to author local motion between them with a collection of motion authoring tools. We evaluate DyCraft on 24 long-horizon, multi-shot animation tasks covering humanoid robots, human and animal characters, and physical mechanisms. Compared with a native GPT-6 agent in Codex and prior agentic baselines, DyCraft substantially reduces physical violations and generates higher-quality animated 3D scenes that are more often preferred by human raters.

papers.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
papers.brief: WikiTrace把经验要点、成败原因摘要和原始轨迹分层链接。智能体遇到信息不足、经验冲突或失败任务经验时，用终端工具追溯证据并修正判断。
papers.tldr: 将经验记忆链接到原始任务证据，让智能体行动前核查，减少记忆误导。
papers.what_it_is: WikiTrace把经验要点、成败原因摘要和原始轨迹分层链接。智能体遇到信息不足、经验冲突或失败任务经验时，用终端工具追溯证据并修正判断。
key_points: WikiTrace以经验要点、成败摘要、原始轨迹组织记忆
信息不足、经验冲突或来自失败任务时，触发证据追溯
在5个智能体基准上优于现有记忆方法及仅用相同要点的基线
papers.why_notable: 它将记忆从直接采信的经验变成可核查的证据入口，为智能体减少错误经验、误读与误用造成的性能退化提供了实证支持。
papers.abstract: External memory enables LLM agents to improve from experience by distilling trajectories of past tasks into concise lessons for new tasks. However, memory can also lead to memory-induced degradation, where an agent fails on tasks it would solve without memory, often because it follows a lesson that is incorrect, or misapplies or misreads a valid one. This is because lessons are inferred from trajectories labeled only with task success or failure, yet are typically provided without the trajectories they came from, leaving the agent no way to check them. To address this, we introduce WikiTrace, an evidence-linked memory system designed to let agents check each lesson against its original trajectory. Specifically, motivated by the finding that a trajectory often still holds the evidence needed to catch an erroneous lesson, WikiTrace stores each lesson as a concise insight linked to a summary of why its trajectory succeeded or failed and to the raw trajectory itself. Then, on a new task, the agent starts from all insights and, whenever one lacks details needed to act, conflicts with another, or comes from a failed task, descends through its links with terminal tools to fill in missing details or correct the insight before acting. We validate WikiTrace on five agentic benchmarks, showing that it consistently outperforms existing memory approaches and a baseline given the same insights alone, while also reducing memory-induced degradation. Our code is available at https://github.com/yukyeongleee/wikitrace

papers.title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
papers.brief: PhysOPSD将真实物理场景转为可验证的仿真程序，作为视频生成的特权上下文。通过双层物理特权与共享噪声下的受控变化，为同策略自蒸馏提供纠正反馈。
papers.tldr: 以可执行仿真代码指导视频模型自蒸馏，用少量样本提升生成动态的物理合理性。
papers.what_it_is: PhysOPSD将真实物理场景转为可验证的仿真程序，作为视频生成的特权上下文。通过双层物理特权与共享噪声下的受控变化，为同策略自蒸馏提供纠正反馈。
key_points: PhysOPSD-Engine将物理场景转为可验证仿真程序
双层物理特权通过中间瓶颈弥合信息差
仅用3K样本超越SFT与RL基线，保持生成质量
papers.why_notable: 把代码的可控性引入物理视频后训练，减少对物理奖励设计的依赖；跨骨干模型的提升显示了这一训练路径的潜力。
papers.abstract: While modern video generative models achieve remarkable visual fidelity, they remain noticeably brittle when generating physically plausible dynamics and complex interactions. Targeted post-training is crucial, yet supervised fine-tuning suffers from offline state mismatch, and reinforcement learning is hindered by sparse, ill-defined physical reward functions. On-Policy (Self-)Distillation (OPSD) reconciles on-policy rollouts with dense corrective feedback, shifting the core challenge to designing effective privileged context. However, conventional modalities fall short: text prompts are inherently declarative, whereas real reference videos heavily entangle physical laws with visual appearance without parametric control. To this end, we propose PhysOPSD, introducing executable code as privileged physical context for video generation. Unlike static visual observations, executable code instantiates an editable physical world with intrinsic abstraction and controllability. Powered by PhysOPSD-Engine, we translate real-world physical scenarios into verifiable simulation programs. PhysOPSD then incorporates (i) dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap via an intermediate bottleneck, alongside (ii) controlled physical variations under shared rollout noise to expose causal dynamic shifts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysOPSD substantially improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones, outperforming SFT and RL baselines with only $3$K samples, while preserving general video generation quality.

papers.title: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting
papers.brief: 将APEX扩展至流式视频生成：原始文本条件用于生成，偏移条件用于估计生成分布的速度场，共享参数替代DMD独立伪评分网络，保留冻结教师与回放训练。
papers.tldr: 通过条件偏移共享生成与分布估计网络，降低少步流式视频训练成本并改善指令遵循。
papers.what_it_is: 将APEX扩展至流式视频生成：原始文本条件用于生成，偏移条件用于估计生成分布的速度场，共享参数替代DMD独立伪评分网络，保留冻结教师与回放训练。
key_points: 条件偏移替代独立伪评分网络，显存降4.4%、迭代耗时降9.2%
评测180秒视频，每块3次骨干评估加单步空间Refiner
70例人工评测中，指令遵循净偏好提升30.0%
papers.why_notable: 把分布估计并入生成器，在降低训练开销的同时改善长视频指令遵循与美感；但运动质量仍落后于对照方法。
papers.abstract: Few-step sampling reduces the cost of streaming video generation. Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) supervises few-step generators with a separate fake-score network, which adds training memory and computation and must track the evolving generator. We extend APEX to streaming video by using condition shifting to estimate the velocity field of the generated distribution within the generator. The original text condition selects generation, while a shifted condition selects fake estimation using the same parameters. This removes the independent fake network while retaining S2-Avatar's frozen reference teacher, Self-Replay Forcing, and perceptual regularization. We evaluate APEX on 180-second videos using three backbone evaluations per block and a one-step spatial Refiner, with a 70-case human study and a 320-case StreamAV-Bench comparison. Compared with S2-Avatar, APEX achieves higher video instruction fulfillment on the Progressive track (3.856 versus 3.831) and higher visual aesthetics across both tracks (0.641898 versus 0.632606). Human raters favor APEX most strongly on instruction following, with +30.0% net preference, followed by consistency and video quality at +4.3% each. Motion quality favors S2-Avatar, audiovisual synchronization is predominantly tied, and usability is unchanged. Separate measurements under matched training settings show 4.4% lower peak allocated GPU memory per GPU and 9.2% shorter mean iteration time than DMD.

papers.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
papers.brief: 提出世界上下文学习WICL，并以RoboScript实现：冻结模型从单次示范出发，在仿真中演练并将反馈写入任务记忆，再迁移至新场景。
papers.tldr: 让冻结模型通过仿真演练积累上下文记忆，单次示范即可学习并迁移机器人操作
papers.what_it_is: 提出世界上下文学习WICL，并以RoboScript实现：冻结模型从单次示范出发，在仿真中演练并将反馈写入任务记忆，再迁移至新场景。
key_points: WICL将演练反馈写入上下文，全程无梯度更新
RoboTwin 2.0全部50项任务平均成功率83.4%
经跨本体记忆适配，迁移到实体双臂机器人
papers.why_notable: 每任务仅用一次示范，成功率仍超过最强训练式动作策略20个百分点以上，展示了以可迁移记忆替代权重更新的潜力。
papers.abstract: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

papers.title: Blind Variation, Selective Retention: Improving Creative Idea Generation in AI Scientists
papers.brief: 提出BVSR框架，将创意生成与候选筛选分开：生成时刻意限制任务信息以拓宽探索，筛选时学习同任务既往提案及实验结果，保留值得验证的候选。
papers.tldr: 通过限制构思信息、利用历史实验筛选，提升AI科学家的创意与发现质量。
papers.what_it_is: 提出BVSR框架，将创意生成与候选筛选分开：生成时刻意限制任务信息以拓宽探索，筛选时学习同任务既往提案及实验结果，保留值得验证的候选。
key_points: 在5个提案模型、12项科学任务上评估BVSR
限制任务信息，提升原创性与非显而易见性
学习历史结果，剔除一半候选并保留多数高表现提案
papers.why_notable: 它表明更多任务信息未必带来更好的科学创意；分阶段使用信息，可兼顾探索多样性与实验筛选效率，并改善多个领域的发现质量。
papers.abstract: Scientific discovery requires ideas that are original, useful, and non-obvious. Yet AI scientists are typically given as much task information as possible during idea generation, which can anchor generation toward familiar approaches. Inspired by the cognitive framework of Blind Variation and Selective Retention (BVSR), we propose a discovery framework that separates these two roles of information: it generates proposals under deliberately limited task information to broaden exploration, then learns from proposals previously verified on the same task and their outcomes to retain promising candidates for costly empirical evaluation. We evaluate BVSR across five proposer models and 12 scientific tasks. Limiting task information substantially increases proposal originality and non-obviousness, and produces a larger share of highly creative and high-utility proposals than existing state-of-the-art prompting-based baselines. Learning from prior proposal outcomes on the task further improves candidate selection, discarding half of the candidates while retaining most top-performing proposals. When incorporated into existing AI-scientist workflows, BVSR achieves stronger discoveries across gene expression analysis, drug response prediction, anomaly detection, scaling law discovery, and brain activity prediction. These results suggest that effective AI scientists should use information differently across stages of discovery: constrain task-specific information during exploration while exploiting accumulated empirical experience on the task.

papers.title: Embodied First Exam
papers.brief: 提出面向编码智能体的机器人评测框架，允许自主选择直接控制、编写控制代码或训练策略，并通过标准、实时与特权设置检验物理约束下的表现。
papers.tldr: 用统一机器人考场检验编码智能体，最强模型在标准设置下成功率仅为34%。
papers.what_it_is: 提出面向编码智能体的机器人评测框架，允许自主选择直接控制、编写控制代码或训练策略，并通过标准、实时与特权设置检验物理约束下的表现。
key_points: 覆盖1156项任务、35个套件和47种机器人
标准设置默认禁重置，实时变体在推理时持续运行
8个智能体参评，456项核心任务最高成功率34%
papers.why_notable: 将机器人评测从视觉运动策略扩展到编码智能体，并用受限观测、实时运行和失败阶段标注，揭示其走向物理世界的能力缺口。
papers.abstract: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints. We therefore introduce the Embodied First Exam, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluation framework where coding agents can choose their own control approach: direct control, code to control, or train a policy to control. We hope it serves as a first exam for coding agents before they enter the physical world, with 1,156 tasks in 35 suites on 47 robots, including 9 new suites that go beyond pick-and-place to spatial puzzles, dexterous manipulation, multi-robot interaction, dynamic whole-body control, and sim-to-sim engineering. Each task can be run in up to three evaluation settings. The Standard Setting mimics the real world: the agent receives only sensor observations and, by default, cannot reset the environment. Its Realtime variant keeps the environment running while the agent reasons. The Privileged Setting gives the agent access to the full simulator state and unlimited resets, allowing it to search for an oracle solution for training purposes. Success rates in this setting serve as an approximate upper bound. On the 456 core tasks, the strongest of eight agents, GPT-6 Astra in Codex, achieves a success rate of 34% in the Standard Setting, leaving much room for improvement. To see where agents fail, we label the stage at which failed attempts go wrong and compare failures across agents, settings, and stage categories.

papers.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
papers.brief: 提出基于原始多传感器卫星档案的地表变化分析基准，让智能体自行去云、协调传感器差异，并通过隐藏参考与对照实验检验答案依据。
papers.tldr: 四十年卫星原始影像评测显示，多模态智能体能完成分析却易误判真实地表变化。
papers.what_it_is: 提出基于原始多传感器卫星档案的地表变化分析基准，让智能体自行去云、协调传感器差异，并通过隐藏参考与对照实验检验答案依据。
key_points: 覆盖56个站点、四十年影像及238道题、十类任务
闭卷与单星数据扰动对照，区分先验和影像依赖
评测12个智能体，扰动使半数正确答案随之改变
papers.why_notable: 把评测从精选图像推进到原始遥感档案，揭示依赖像素并不等于识别真实地表变化，为智能体可靠性提供更严格检验。
papers.abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. Two controls test what answers rest on: the closed book removes the record, and instrument pairs alter one satellite's data while nothing changes on the ground. Evaluations of twelve multimodal agents reveal that leading agents complete most analyses end to end but falter when an answer requires mapping from imagery. Further analysis shows that the record moves answers from prior knowledge to the pixels but not yet to the real change on the ground: when one satellite's data are altered, half of the right answers follow the alteration. EarthRecord thus provides a principled platform for measuring and advancing agents from pixels to land change.

papers.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
papers.brief: Tree-Ising利用前向统计构建修复目标，在BF16权重上做符号翻转与指数移位，再精确分解为逐行独立的QUBO问题，用GPU求解。
papers.tldr: 将权重位级修复转化为离散优化，以低成本缓解语言模型推理循环并提升数学表现。
papers.what_it_is: Tree-Ising利用前向统计构建修复目标，在BF16权重上做符号翻转与指数移位，再精确分解为逐行独立的QUBO问题，用GPU求解。
key_points: 模拟退火修复后MATH-500达54.6%，优于智能体的51.7%
仅需4次前向请求、零LLM词元，退火GPU成本约0.90美元
Qwen3.5-2B的GSM8K准确率从21.6%升至69.4%
papers.why_notable: 将昂贵的智能体权重修复替换为可分解的离散求解，在减少修改权重和位翻转的同时提升数学表现，展示了无梯度修复的效率潜力。
papers.abstract: Weight-space programming, introduced in recent MIT work by Takehi et al., enables a frontier LLM agent to read a network's weights and write a repair. Their GPT-6 Astra agent corrected the reasoning loops of Qwen3.5-0.8B without gradients, using 158 agent turns, 89.7 million tokens, and 50 forward-pass requests. Our method, Tree-Ising, casts this repair as a sparse discrete optimization problem over the model's own BF16 weights. Forward statistics define an objective that weakens a loop direction, strengthens a concluding direction, and preserves the layer's output on productive tokens. Within a state-tree representation, where lossless BF16 storage acts as a special case, the admissible edits are sign flips and exponent shifts that preserve all shared group exponents and mantissas. We decompose this objective exactly into independent QUBO (Ising) problems, one per output row, which we solve on a GPU using simulated annealing or quantum-inspired simulated bifurcation. On the agent's two layers, Tree-Ising achieves 54.6% on MATH-500, outperforming the agent's edit (51.7%) under the same evaluation protocol, while the base model scores 7.9% as reported. The simulated bifurcation solver yields a statistically indistinguishable repair at 55.1%. Both solvers outperform the agent edit across all five math benchmarks, with statistically significant improvements on MATH-500 and GSM8K after correcting for multiple comparisons. Our approach modifies 13% to 17% fewer weights and reduces BF16 bit flips by a factor of 2.2 to 2.3. It requires only four forward-pass requests and zero LLM tokens, with the annealing recipe costing about $0.90 in GPU time. On Qwen3.5-2B, with layers and dose selected using only the base model, the same recipe increases greedy GSM8K accuracy from 21.6% to 69.4%. As a proof of concept, we execute an eight-variable repair subproblem using QAOA on an IBM Heron processor.

papers.title: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next
papers.brief: WM-PPO用世界模型预测采样动作的后继观察，再由价值网络评估，构造策略辅助优势与价值辅助目标；共享门控按历史预测可靠性调节两者权重。
papers.tldr: 世界模型预测动作后果，价值网络评估成功概率，提升稀疏奖励下的智能体学习效率。
papers.what_it_is: WM-PPO用世界模型预测采样动作的后继观察，再由价值网络评估，构造策略辅助优势与价值辅助目标；共享门控按历史预测可靠性调节两者权重。
key_points: WM-PPO同时评估已执行与未执行的采样动作
ALFWorld成功率从63.5%升至87.5%
ScienceWorld成功率从39.3%升至52.9%
papers.why_notable: 在相近真实交互步数下，将动作后果预测转化为稀疏奖励之外的学习信号；无需教师或特权信息，推理时仅使用策略。
papers.abstract: A sparse terminal reward tells an agent little about its steps. Much of the missing information is implicit in the environment's dynamics, because each state transition can change the conditions for success long before the reward arrives. A world model trained on real transitions can learn to predict what each action changes, but a predicted observation does not by itself show whether success has become more likely. With a binary terminal reward, PPO's critic makes this judgment by estimating the current policy's probability of success, but only for states the agent reaches. Our method, WM-PPO, elegantly brings the two together. For each action the policy samples, executed or not, the world model predicts the next observation and the critic values the predicted successor. In the policy channel, comparisons among these values give the policy auxiliary advantages; in the value channel, their mean gives the critic an auxiliary target. A shared gate weights both channels according to how reliably comparisons with similar margins predicted real outcomes earlier in training. The policy, critic and world model all learn from the agent's own interaction, with no teacher or privileged information, and only the policy is used at inference. With a comparable number of real environment steps, WM-PPO raises success from PPO's 63.5% to 87.5% on ALFWorld and from 39.3% to 52.9% on ScienceWorld. It matches the strongest PPO refinements we tested on ALFWorld and exceeds the best of them by 6.5 points on ScienceWorld. The trained policy more often completes prerequisite steps before placing an object or committing to an answer.

papers.title: Micius-Flash: Lightweight Agentic Intelligence for Engineering
papers.brief: 这是一个支持原生多模态输入、深度推理和长上下文的工程模型。它用知识树驱动数据合成与校验，再通过多教师在线策略蒸馏整合领域专家能力。
papers.tldr: 通过多教师蒸馏整合工程专家能力，让轻量模型胜任半导体设计与工具协作。
papers.what_it_is: 这是一个支持原生多模态输入、深度推理和长上下文的工程模型。它用知识树驱动数据合成与校验，再通过多教师在线策略蒸馏整合领域专家能力。

MOPD在模型自生成序列上融合多类专家能力
硬件代码得分64.2%，智能体得分62.4%
papers.why_notable: 两类工程基准分别领先同规模基线15.0和17.2个百分点；开源模型配套工具框架，可连接EDA与KiCad开展迭代验证。
papers.abstract: We introduce Micius-Flash, a 27-billion-parameter model for engineering with native multimodal input, deep reasoning and a 256K-token context window. We design the Micius data pipeline as a knowledge-tree-driven data flywheel comprising three stages: knowledge tree construction and expansion, data synthesis, and quality validation with hard-example augmentation. From this data, we train expert models for semiconductor knowledge and reasoning, hardware coding, and semiconductor multimodal understanding, along with agentic experts. Subsequently, we employ Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) to supervise training on sequences generated by Micius itself, thereby integrating the capabilities of these expert models into a unified model. On more than 20 datasets with about 15K records, Micius-Flash averages 64.2% on hardware code benchmarks, 15.0 points above a same-size baseline. It scores 62.4% on a semiconductor-specific agent benchmark, exceeding the same-size baseline by 17.2 points. We further develop Micius Harness for industrial applications, connecting the model to specialized tools, including EDA tools and KiCad, as well as execution environments. Case studies in PCB design, chip design workflow automation, and software development demonstrate the model's ability to use tool execution feedback for multi-step planning, code debugging, and iterative verification. We release Micius as an open-source model to advance the development of agents for science and engineering.

papers.title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
papers.brief: 研究提出闭环安全基准RoboRisk与防护框架LEASH。后者借助决策模型，在视觉上下文中审查任务、动作及不可逆操作，并与规划器共享安全策略。
papers.tldr: 以闭环机器人安全基准与三重决策门控，降低智能体执行任务的伤害风险。
papers.what_it_is: 研究提出闭环安全基准RoboRisk与防护框架LEASH。后者借助决策模型，在视觉上下文中审查任务、动作及不可逆操作，并与规划器共享安全策略。
key_points: RoboRisk含92项仿真、13项真机任务，覆盖五类风险
LEASH设置任务、动作、提交三道安全门控
六种基础模型接入后伤害减少，任务完成表现大体保留
papers.why_notable: 将安全评估从文本输出推进到闭环机器人执行，并提供可跨智能体架构集成的防护机制，在降低伤害的同时保持较低额外开销。
papers.abstract: Foundation models such as GPT and Claude have shown strong capabilities in spatial understanding and embodied intelligence. These advances make agentic robotics a promising path toward artificial general intelligence in robotics. However, we find that using foundation models to control robots poses serious safety risks, and comprehensive safety evaluation is still lacking. We introduce RoboRisk, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating safety in agentic robotics. Its 92 simulated tasks and 13 physical-robot tasks fall into five categories: Task-level Refusal (T), Plan Repair (P), Execution-time Hazard (E), Injection (I), and Sequential Memory (S). Prior benchmarks cover at most two of these categories, and several evaluate only text outputs. In contrast, RoboRisk covers all five and executes every task in closed loop. We evaluate six state-of-the-art foundation models on RoboRisk: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, and Grok 4.7. These models generally show high harm rates. We also evaluate two robot-specific APIs: the Dream API and PokeBot's RoboAPI. We further propose the Lease-Enforced Agentic Safety Harness (LEASH), which offers essential safety infrastructure for agentic robotics and can be integrated into nearly any agentic architecture. LEASH leverages a decision model (Jev or OpenAI's Decisions API) to implement task, action, and commit gates, which review the task, each action, and each irreversible operation in their visual context. The planner and all three gates share a common safety policy. Experiments on RoboRisk in simulation and on physical robots show that LEASH effectively reduces harm across all six foundation models. It largely preserves their task completion performance and adds little time and token overhead.

papers.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
papers.brief: 提出 Contrastive Discovery，将科学问题与互斥且完备的解释集合绑定。按实验证据引起的信念重分配评分，既可重评已有证据，也可引导后续搜索。
papers.tldr: 用互斥且完备的竞争解释替代单假设检验，让科学发现智能体更有效地确定答案。
papers.what_it_is: 提出 Contrastive Discovery，将科学问题与互斥且完备的解释集合绑定。按实验证据引起的信念重分配评分，既可重评已有证据，也可引导后续搜索。
key_points: 六个领域中，信念变化最大的单假设候选有89%被否定
相同证据下，竞争解释集将73%的上述候选确定为具体替代解释
相同实验预算下，引导搜索比单假设惊异度多解决67%的问题
papers.why_notable: 把否定假设转化为确定替代解释，提高证据和实验预算的利用率；38名专家盲评中，对已解决问题的解释一致率达78%。
papers.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation. Because contrast sets change only the unit an agent proposes and scores, an existing agent can use them to re-evaluate evidence it has already collected or to guide its search. Across six domains, $89\%$ of the pointwise candidates with the largest belief shifts are rejections. On the same evidence, contrast sets resolve $73\%$ of these candidates to a specific alternative. When contrast sets guide search, the agent resolves $67\%$ more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget. In a blinded study, $38$ human experts chose the same explanation on $78\%$ of resolved questions and on $82\%$ of questions where the pointwise agent rejected its hypothesis and stopped. Together, these results support explicit competing explanations as a way for discovery agents to resolve more scientific questions from the same evidence and validation budget.

papers.title: Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via On-Policy Distillation
papers.brief: 构建覆盖五类任务的长程智能体环境，以普通Bash和持久工作区承载文件记忆。再用全异步策略内蒸馏，让单一策略向冻结教师学习记忆读写。
papers.tldr: 通过策略内蒸馏激活文件操作先验，让智能体学会跨上下文管理长期记忆。
papers.what_it_is: 构建覆盖五类任务的长程智能体环境，以普通Bash和持久工作区承载文件记忆。再用全异步策略内蒸馏，让单一策略向冻结教师学习记忆读写。
key_points: CAMG-II覆盖购物、编程等五类长程任务
CAMP-II以全异步OPD学习文件记忆操作
增益为最强OPD基线的2.97倍，并迁移至两项外部基准
papers.why_notable: 将记忆接口对齐模型已有的文件操作能力，改善蒸馏指导与探索效率；外部编程基准的成功率提升显示了迁移价值。
papers.abstract: Language-model agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks whose interaction histories exceed the model's active context. They must therefore decide what to write down and what to read back, and when to do either. Recent work has begun to use on-policy distillation (OPD) to make memory control part of the policy, relying on memory tools and compaction protocols that lie outside either model's pre-training. However, this weakens the distillation on both sides: the teacher cannot give useful guidance on an interface it has never used, and the student samples too few meaningful memory actions for that guidance to take effect. To study this problem, we introduce Coding Agent Memory Gym II (CAMG-II), a suite of long-horizon agentic-RL environments spanning Shop, Coding, AutoResearch, General, and Visual. Alongside each environment's native task interface, CAMG-II provides ordinary Bash access and an episode-persistent workspace, enabling the policy to create, revise, search, and reuse files as memory across context replacements. We also introduce Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II (CAMP-II), which trains a single policy jointly across all five environments with fully asynchronous OPD to learn this file-based memory behavior directly from a frozen teacher with a prior for file operations. On CAMG-II, CAMP-II obtains 2.97 times the gain of the strongest OPD baseline. The memory behavior CAMP-II learns generalizes to two external benchmarks, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Pro V2, with improved success rates.

papers.title: MACaQ: Fast, Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization for Low-Precision Weights and Activations
papers.brief: MACaQ是权重与激活均为四比特的训练后量化方法，逐层在线执行通道缩放和分块Hadamard变换，并将逆变换吸收入权重，配合精度细化降低误差。
papers.tldr: 以逐层独立变换和精度细化，实现低内存、快速且跨架构的四比特量化。
papers.what_it_is: MACaQ是权重与激活均为四比特的训练后量化方法，逐层在线执行通道缩放和分块Hadamard变换，并将逆变换吸收入权重，配合精度细化降低误差。
key_points: Flip-Refinement以Hessian感知坐标下降调整FP4编码
Llama-3-8B匹配对手最佳困惑度，量化快11倍
122B模型量化耗时64分钟，仅需32.5GB显存
papers.why_notable: 逐层独立设计摆脱跨层变换依赖，可直接用于图像扩散模型；Qwen3-32B推理额外开销仅2.3%，兼顾通用性与效率。
papers.abstract: Weight-activation quantization can reduce the memory and compute cost of neural-network inference, but recent methods often require expensive optimization and architecture-specific propagation of basis transforms across layers. We introduce MACaQ, an MXFP4 W4A4 post-training quantization method that treats every linear layer independently. MACaQ applies a per-channel scale and a block-Hadamard transform online to each layer's activations, while absorbing the corresponding inverse transforms into its weights. Retaining these transforms online avoids cross-layer dependencies and enables a simple streaming implementation of the quantization process, in which only one layer must reside in memory at a time. To improve over round-to-nearest quantization, we introduce Flip-Refinement, a Hessian-aware coordinate-descent procedure that greedily moves individual FP4 codes to adjacent representable values. Despite executing the activation transforms at inference time, MACaQ adds only 2.3% end-to-end overhead over pure MXFP4 on Qwen3-32B in vLLM. MACaQ reaches lower perplexity than DuQuant++ and MR-GPTQ, and already matches their best perplexity on Llama-3-8B in 11 times less quantization time. We further apply MACaQ without architecture-specific modifications to an image diffusion model, illustrating the generality of its layer-local design and show quantization of a 122B parameter model in 64 minutes, using only 32.5GB GPU RAM.

papers.title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
papers.brief: WaveGen以Spectral Forcing联合学习内部频谱与波形轨迹，并在模型内完成文本语音对齐。通过解耦扩散头和多尺度频谱损失，实现单阶段训练。
papers.tldr: 用单一扩散模型直接从文本生成语音波形，无需外部声码器与对齐模块。
papers.what_it_is: WaveGen以Spectral Forcing联合学习内部频谱与波形轨迹，并在模型内完成文本语音对齐。通过解耦扩散头和多尺度频谱损失，实现单阶段训练。
key_points: Spectral Forcing联合学习频谱与波形轨迹
采用解耦扩散头与多尺度频谱v损失
Seed-en上WER为1.47，SIM为0.75
papers.why_notable: 将语音生成、频谱建模和对齐收进单一模型，减少多模块依赖；参数从1亿扩至6亿，验证端到端路线的扩展潜力。
papers.abstract: This work proposes WaveGen, a fully end-to-end diffusion-based text-to-waveform framework based on Spectral Forcing, which jointly learns an internal spectral trajectory and the target waveform trajectory within a single model, enabling direct end-to-end text-to-waveform generation. Unlike recent TTS pipelines, WaveGen does not rely on separately trained or externally decoded intermediate representations, such as neural audio codecs, Mel-spectrogram vocoders, or VAE-based latent models. In addition, WaveGen performs internal text-speech alignment within a single model, eliminating the need for external alignment modules such as duration predictors. To preserve a truly end-to-end formulation, our framework further avoids dependence on self-supervised representations, such as BERT-based text embeddings and Wav2Vec 2.0-based semantic representations, as well as semantic distillation methods for training optimization. To achieve this, we carefully design Spectral Forcing, a model architecture with disentangled diffusion heads, and a training objective based on a multi-scale spectral $v$-loss. We further validate the scalability of end-to-end TTS models by scaling the model size from 0.1B to 0.6B parameters. Using a single architecture, open-source data, and one-stage training, without external modules such as duration predictor or REPA, WaveGen demonstrates fully end-to-end waveform generation achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Emilia training dataset. In particular, WaveGen achieves a WER of 1.47 and a SIM of 0.75 on the Seed-en benchmark. Source code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/sh-lee-prml/WaveGen

papers.title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
papers.brief: dNaViT是原生分辨率视觉分词器，在冻结编码器上以轻量残差调制和双分支目标融合语义与重建信息，再通过分组乘积量化生成离散编码。
papers.tldr: 用紧凑离散视觉词表兼顾语义理解与高保真重建，统一多类视觉任务编码。
papers.what_it_is: dNaViT是原生分辨率视觉分词器，在冻结编码器上以轻量残差调制和双分支目标融合语义与重建信息，再通过分组乘积量化生成离散编码。
key_points: 冻结预训练编码器，以残差调制和双分支目标兼顾语义与重建。
分组乘积量化扩大离散容量，不增加空间序列长度。
在12项理解、4项生成及1项编辑基准上达到或超过专用基线。
papers.why_notable: 同一离散编码兼顾视觉理解、生成与编辑，为视觉和语言共享词元建模范式及基础设施提供了更有力的实证支持。
papers.abstract: Discrete autoregressive modeling, notably through next-token prediction, has become a cornerstone of modern language models. Extending this paradigm to vision allows visual and language models to converge on a unified framework, thereby fostering shared methodology and infrastructure. This work investigates a central question: how far can a finite discrete vocabulary go in representing the richness of the visual world? We present dNaViT, a Discrete Native-resolution Vision Transformer that produces discrete visual primitives analogous to language tokens. Built upon a frozen pretrained encoder, dNaViT applies lightweight residual modulation with a dual-branch objective to inject reconstruction-aware cues into semantic features. By leveraging grouped product quantization, it scales discrete capacity without inflating spatial sequence lengths, while a balanced training recipe maintains both semantic and pixel-level information. Consequently, dNaViT functions as a versatile discrete visual tokenizer, enabling unified encoding across downstream tasks alongside high-fidelity image decoding. Extensive evaluations show that dNaViT matches or exceeds task-specific baselines across 12 visual understanding benchmarks, 4 generation benchmarks, and an image editing benchmark. These findings demonstrate that a compact discrete vocabulary can serve as a universal visual currency and unlock the full potential of fully unified, native multimodal methodology.

papers.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
papers.brief: Deletion Tuning在Transformer块的门控投影上学习二值掩码，仅将少量权重置零，不改动其余权重，即可获得新能力。
papers.tldr: 仅将不到万分之五的权重置零，就能在三类大模型后训练中匹敌全量微调。
papers.what_it_is: Deletion Tuning在Transformer块的门控投影上学习二值掩码，仅将少量权重置零，不改动其余权重，即可获得新能力。
key_points: 置零不足0.05%权重，在三类后训练中匹敌FFT
掩码比FFT检查点小数百至数千倍
强化学习中旧任务准确率近基线，对照最多降5.4点
papers.why_notable: 它表明获取新能力未必需要更新权重数值，并以更小存储开销和更少遗忘，为低成本后训练与持续学习提供新路径。
papers.abstract: How little of a pretrained large language model (LLM) has to change for it to acquire new capabilities? We find that zeroing fewer than 0.05% of its weights, with no other modification, matches full fine-tuning (FFT) at scale across three LLM post-training regimes: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, supervised fine-tuning, and on-policy distillation. Our method, Deletion Tuning, learns a binary mask over the gate projection of transformer blocks. Two practical advantages follow: the trained mask is hundreds to thousands of times smaller than the corresponding FFT checkpoint, and Deletion Tuning forgets far less, which addresses a central challenge in continual learning. Under reinforcement learning, its prior-task accuracy stays near the base level while FFT, LoRA, and random sparse fine-tuning lose up to 5.4 points. To understand why masking alone suffices, we analyze the geometry of the learned weight changes under reinforcement learning using stable rank, spectrum drift, and principal-weight overlap. Compared with LoRA and random sparse fine-tuning, Deletion Tuning is closest to FFT across the three measures.

papers.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
papers.brief: 构建金融智能体开放世界评测：模拟用户按询问披露隐藏策略，智能体自行联网取数并回测。无需参考答案，以策略匹配、时点核验和指标重算验证交付结果。
papers.tldr: 用开放网络、隐藏策略与时点核验，揭示金融智能体看似可信的隐性失败。
papers.what_it_is: 构建金融智能体开放世界评测：模拟用户按询问披露隐藏策略，智能体自行联网取数并回测。无需参考答案，以策略匹配、时点核验和指标重算验证交付结果。
key_points: 用户满意且通过全部15项否决检查才算成功
4个编码智能体及1个无工具模型，150次会话零通过
借助评测反馈与持久记忆，智能体学会全部10项任务
papers.why_notable: 把需求澄清、数据真实性和未来信息泄漏纳入统一验收，揭示用户认可不等于结果正确，也为智能体持续改进提供可验证反馈。
papers.abstract: Language agents increasingly work for users on the open Web, and finance is where trusting them is hardest. The data must come from the Web, the strategy lives in the user's head, and correctness depends on time, so an agent can fail silently: a strategy the user never asked for, unverified data, or a backtest that uses the future yields a report as convincing as a correct one. Existing benchmarks close the world somewhere, fixing the task, the data, or the timeline, and thereby remove these failures instead of measuring them. We introduce FINCOSMOS, an open-world evaluation paradigm for agents doing financial work. A simulated user holds a hidden strategy sampled from a compositional grammar and reveals it only when asked. The agent receives no data, so it must acquire data from the Web, build its own backtest under a data cutoff, and deliver verifiable results. Grading needs no reference answer. Programs verify point-in-time correctness and recompute every reported metric, the delivered strategy is checked against the hidden specification, and a run is accepted only when the user is satisfied and none of 15 veto checks fails. Across four coding agents and a model without tools in 150 sessions, no session is accepted: every session that the simulated user signed off fails a program check, and agents raise only 54--64\% of the details they were not told. Human experts attribute 88.33\% of failures to the agents. With FINCOSMOS feedback, an agent with persistent memory learned all ten tasks.

papers.title: MMDM: Measuring Massive Multitask Decision Making
papers.brief: MMDM用新构建任务与基于来源的重组改写，评估单次前向输出选项概率的决策模型。它覆盖单选、多选和软标签决策，同时考察长上下文、大选项空间与逻辑依赖。
papers.tldr: 新基准联合测试长上下文与复杂选项，揭示决策模型在约束和多选上的短板。
papers.what_it_is: MMDM用新构建任务与基于来源的重组改写，评估单次前向输出选项概率的决策模型。它覆盖单选、多选和软标签决策，同时考察长上下文、大选项空间与逻辑依赖。
key_points: MMDM含5,448题、16类任务，评测28个决策模型。
选项数为2至1,024，输入最长64,817词元。
所有模型中，最高硬多选准确率仅36.81%。
papers.why_notable: 它将通常分开评估的长输入、大选项空间与约束推理放到同一测试框架中，更清楚地区分知识熟悉度与复杂决策能力。
papers.abstract: System-1 Decision Models directly make structured probabilistic decisions over query-specified options given a state in a single forward pass, without autoregressively generating reasoning trajectories or textual responses. Recent evaluations cover diverse tasks but often rely on existing benchmarks, where prior exposure to test material can obscure generalization. Moreover, real-world decision making often involves long contexts, large option spaces, and complex logical dependencies, challenges that existing benchmarks do not adequately capture together. Thus, we introduce MMDM (Massive Multitask Decision Making), a benchmark of 5,448 high-quality questions across 16 task categories, combining newly constructed tasks with source-grounded recompositions and rewrites for single-select, multi-select, and soft-label decision making in fresh contexts. It covers realistic scenarios such as agent state tracking, tool and skill selection, preference judgments, and rubric scoring, with option spaces ranging from 2 to 1,024 and inputs extending to 64,817 tokens. With MMDM, we conduct a comprehensive quantitative evaluation of 28 decision models, showing that many perform well on common knowledge yet struggle with interdependent options, constrained decisions, and multi-select tasks. For example, Perplexity Decider-V1.2 reaches 78.75% Hard Single-select Accuracy on world knowledge, but only 53.95% on option logic and 47.95% on constraint planning, while the best Hard Multi-select Accuracy across all models is 36.81%. These results highlight joint reasoning, constraint-aware selection, and complete multi-select recovery as key priorities for decision model development, with MMDM providing a testbed for measuring this progress.
papers.organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong - Database Group

papers.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
papers.abstract: Rapidly evolving LLM architectures and heterogeneous mobile hardware make supporting new models in on-device inference engines a recurring and costly system challenge. Each model may require coordinated changes across conversion, graph construction, operators, and hardware backends. Existing coding agents often miss these cross-layer dependencies and struggle to diagnose failures across host--device execution paths. We present EngineAgent, an agentic system for automating on-device LLM model enablement. Its key insight is to separate reusable engine and hardware knowledge from model-specific implementation. Before enablement, EngineAgent constructs a hierarchy-aware engine index that captures engine abstraction layers and cross-layer dependencies, and pre-validates backend-specific build, execution, and debugging workflows using already supported models. For each new model, a builder uses this knowledge to coordinate cross-layer changes, while an auditor checks implementation completeness and drives iterative debugging through device-side validation. Across 12 tasks spanning three mobile LLMs and four engine--backend pairs on CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, EngineAgent achieves 75% end-to-end success with either of two underlying LLMs, versus 33.3% for the strongest coding-agent baseline. Success requires compilation, on-device execution, and output-logit agreement with reference implementations. EngineAgent also reduces average per-task time and model-API cost relative to baselines using the same underlying LLMs.

papers.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly operate in long-horizon, verifier-rich environments, but current self-improvement mechanisms often write episode-derived lessons directly into memory, making local success an unreliable signal for reusable and safe knowledge. This paper addresses the core question of when an experience-derived behavioral update should be admitted into persistent agent state. We propose Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution (FGSE), a verifier-grounded framework that represents each candidate lesson as a structured hypothesis with an explicit precondition, behavior change, expected effect, and verifier. FGSE applies the hypothesis only in a temporary state, tests it on target-transfer, falsification, and archived-regression probes, and then commits, refines, or rejects it according to measured gain and risk. Across web, app, tool-use, and long-term memory benchmarks, FGSE achieves strong task performance, including 39.8 WebArena success rate, 78.8 AppWorld average completion, and 0.724/0.487 Pass$^1$ on $τ$-Retail/$τ$-Airline, while reducing falsification failures to 5.0%, regression damage to 1.3%, and harmful committed updates to 3.6%. These results suggest that testing memory updates as hypotheses supports more reliable long-term adaptation.

papers.title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
papers.abstract: Software agents built on large language models generate traffic unlike human web traffic, yet routers have no class for it and cannot verify a sender's claim to be an agent. This paper proposes the Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class (VATC), which combines a reserved Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) value declaring agent traffic, a router-side classifier that demotes flows contradicting the declaration to a class served after best-effort traffic, and a rate-limited priority queue. VATC was compared with static Differentiated Services (DiffServ), a dedicated class that trusts the marking, and fq_codel, a per-flow fair-queuing scheduler, in two simulators and on a real Linux kernel. VATC matched DiffServ under steady load. In a constructed burst it cut mean agent queuing delay by 98% relative to DiffServ in simulation (assuming an immediate verdict), at a 12% increase in human delay; most of the gain came from the separate class. Under a spoofed flood in the kernel, the rate limit held human latency 11 times below DiffServ's. Without verification, DiffServ and a tightly configured fq_codel gave legitimate agents lower latency than VATC; a live four-feature classifier then demoted all 20 bulk-shaped spoofers and gave agents 0.30 ms, but missed six spoofers that copied the agent pattern. With emulated network delay, a timing feature of the classifier stopped separating agent from human flows. In real agent harnesses on a congested link, router queueing took 13% to 63% of task time, depending on harness and assumed model latency. The traffic was synthetic or sandbox-scale.

papers.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
papers.abstract: Formal verification using proof assistants provides strong correctness guarantees for software, but constructing proofs remains labor-intensive and requires significant expertise. Recent approaches based on large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in automating proof synthesis. However, these approaches typically constrain the model to a rigid tactic-generation loop, in which the surrounding system controls premise retrieval, proof-state management, and backtracking. We introduce ProofCoder, an agentic proof-synthesis system for Rocq that approaches theorem proving from a coding-agent perspective. Rather than generating tactics within a fixed loop, ProofCoder reasons continuously throughout proof search and uses proof-assistant feedback to decide when to gather additional information, inspect proof states, revise previously generated proof fragments, or backtrack to an earlier point in the proof. This allows it to iteratively construct, repair, and refine proofs, at either tactic-level or whole-proof granularity. We evaluate ProofCoder on 280 challenging verification tasks from the AutoRocq Benchmark. On the best-performing configurations, ProofCoder increases proof success from 47% to 60% over the state-of-theart AutoRocq system, corresponding to a 27.7% relative improvement at approximately half the cost. Our ablations identify continuous reasoning as a key design choice: without it, the agent solves fewer lemmas at substantially higher cost, backtracks four to six times more often, and more frequently discards its own revisions. Whole-proof and tactic-level generation achieve similar success rates but follow distinct search and repair strategies. These results suggest that effective automated software verification requires more than improved tactic selection: continuous reasoning and feedback-guided proof revision are critical ingredients for robust proof synthesis.

papers.title: Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution
papers.abstract: Agent skills have emerged as an effective means of enabling LLM agents to solve complex, interactive tasks by encoding reusable knowledge without modifying model parameters. Recent approaches further improve skill adaptation by distilling reusable experience from agent execution trajectories and evolving skills based on downstream task feedback. However, existing methods primarily represent skills as natural language documents, intertwining procedural logic with descriptive knowledge and making skills difficult to maintain and evolve. To address this limitation, we propose PASE (Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution), a program-aided framework that iteratively evolves skills by associating them with executable programs. Unlike prior approaches that encode trajectory-derived experience primarily in natural language, PASE separates reusable procedural logic into editable programs, enabling targeted updates to executable components while reducing the need to repeatedly revise natural language skills. Extensive experiments across diverse models and benchmarks demonstrate that PASE consistently outperforms all baselines, by achieving over 2.8% improvements. Further analyses show that PASE exhibits greater evolutionary stability and generalisation capability, highlighting the critical role of programmatic knowledge in skill evolution. We will release all data and code via GitHub.

papers.title: Controlled Knowledge Engineering for Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded LLM Agents and Runtime-Adaptive Policies
papers.abstract: Taxonomies are structured knowledge representations that support semantic search, recommendation, product catalog organization, and retrieval-augmented generation. Their automated construction from a fixed set of candidate entities requires more than plausible text generation: the resulting hierarchy must be complete, structurally valid, and semantically coherent. Large Language Models (LLMs) are promising for this task, but iterative free-form generation remains vulnerable to omitted or hallucinated entities, invalid hierarchical relations, and inconsistent organizational principles. We introduce TIGA (Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded Agents), a knowledge-engineering architecture that formulates taxonomy induction as an iterative decision process over an explicit state and constrained action space. TIGA combines executable taxonomy-editing tools, an memory that records tool calls, rationales, and outcomes, and a runtime-adaptive organizational policy that the agent revises during inference. An optional global reviewer evaluates the constructed taxonomy against the candidate set and the active policy. We evaluate TIGA on four benchmark taxonomies using two LLM backbones and compare it with single-shot and iterative prompting-based baselines. TIGA achieves the strongest structural-quality results in most evaluated configurations, but does not dominate on every precision measure. The gains are accompanied by substantially higher token consumption, API-call volume, and inference time. Ablation results show consistent benefits from the policy and interaction-memory components, whereas the effect of global review depends on the dataset and the available revision budget. These findings characterize tool grounding and runtime policy adaptation as promising but costly mechanisms for improving the controlled construction of structured knowledge representations.

papers.title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
papers.abstract: AI coding harnesses couple language models to shells, filesystems, and network sockets, turning the harness into an automated Living-off-the-Land (LotL) platform: once an adversary injects instructions into retrieved content, dual-use binaries such as bash, curl, and find become the payload. We argue that security in agentic systems is a structural property of the cognitive architecture and permission composition rather than an emergent property of individual models. Static regex blacklists miss structural evasions, whereas LLM-as-a-Judge guardrails incur high latency while over-blocking benign work. We present ActiveSecHarness, a neurosymbolic reference-monitor architecture built around Separation of Intelligence and Authority. It combines (1) Macaroon-inspired HMAC capability tokens across four Trust and Authority Rings, (2) a 2D product taint lattice $\mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{trust}} \times \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{sens}}$ and a workspace provenance ledger that prevents secret laundering across disk, (3) deterministic Ring-0 OS/tool guards, and (4) bytecode certificates, split-horizon audit logs, self-healing security test synthesis, and an adaptive UserWikiManager. Across $N=252$ fixtures ($120$ attack, $120$ benign, $12$ kill chains), a live local LLM judge (qwen3:4b) refuses $98.3\%$ of benign work at $142.3\,\mathrm{ms}$ latency, whereas Ring 0 achieves $\mathrm{ABR}=1.000$ and $\mathrm{FPR}=0.000$ in $12.7\,μ\mathrm{s}$ ($11{,}200\times$ faster). In a multi-step trajectory ablation, an oracle Conseca-style stateless policy misses $4/12$ kill chains ($\mathrm{ABR}=0.667$) and coarse Boolean taint blocks $83.3\%$ of benign workflows, while our 2D product lattice achieves $\mathrm{ABR}=1.000$ and $\mathrm{FPR}=0.000$ at $\approx 20\,μ\mathrm{s}$ per step.

papers.title: Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and autonomous agents are creating new opportunities for hardware design optimization. This paper examines three connected directions toward autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization: (1) Realistic benchmarking. We discuss reference-based and open-ended RTL optimization benchmarks that evaluate optimization opportunities under realistic EDA workflows. (2) Tool-grounded RTL optimization. We present Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework that automates critical-path analysis, RTL rewriting, and implementation-level evaluation, while continuously improving through reusable optimization skills. Evaluated on 20 real-world RTL designs, Dr.~RTL achieves average WNS/TNS improvements of 21\%/17\% with a 6\% area reduction over commercial synthesis. (3) Design-specific synthesis optimization. We explore agent-driven synthesis script tuning and the discovery of executable synthesis algorithms across intermediate representations, technology-independent optimization, and technology mapping. Finally, we envision AI-native design automation that jointly explores architectural, RTL, and EDA algorithm design spaces, guided by verification constraints and implementation feedback.

papers.title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
papers.abstract: Manifold embedding for data visualisation is dominated by a small set of hand-designed state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithms. Their design targets are fixed at development time, resulting in inflexible algorithmic behaviour that cannot be readily steered towards user-specified structural priorities. Hand-designing new embedding algorithms to address user priority requires highly specialised expertise and is time consuming. To address autonomous algorithm design tailored to user preference, we introduce an agentic algorithm generation pipeline AutoManifold. It composes new manifold embedding algorithms from a constrained vocabulary of affinity, cost, and optimisation primitives, supported by multi-agent large-language-model (LLM) orchestration. AutoManifold conditions every stage of its design on user-specified structural preservation preferences, and iteratively refines the algorithm configuration through an LLM-guided, metric-grounded iterative loop. We compare the generated algorithms against the three strongest and most frequently used SOTA methods (t-SNE, UMAP, and PaCMAP) on real-world datasets spanning different difficulty regimes under identical evaluation infrastructure. The results demonstrate that LLM-driven, priority-conditioned algorithm synthesis can move beyond hyperparameter tuning, producing genuinely new algorithms that outperform traditional hand-designed methods in their ability to steer towards user-specified properties without compromising the intrinsic structure in the original data. The code of AutoManifold is available at https://github.com/buraksusam/AutoManifold_NeurIPS2026.

papers.title: Agentic AI Meets Formal Verification in the Era of Agentic Hardware Development
papers.abstract: As AI agents become increasingly capable of generating and optimizing hardware circuits, ensuring the correctness of AI-generated designs becomes more important. Meanwhile, advances in AI lower the barriers to developing and applying formal methods, creating new opportunities to automate and improve hardware verification. This invited paper presents an overview of the methodologies and applications of hardware formal methods in the AI era. First, we examine how agentic AI advances hardware formal methods across three levels: specification, proof construction, and reasoning engines. Second, we discuss how formal methods support reliable AI-driven hardware development through RTL generation, debugging, and correctness-preserving optimization. We review representative research alongside our recent contributions, highlighting key technical advances and insights from experimental results. Finally, we discuss future research opportunities toward proof-native hardware development, where formal reasoning could become an integral part of autonomous hardware design.

papers.title: On Private Knowledge Retrieval and Private Inference for secure multi-agent systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems provide a convenient framework for the massive deployment of agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs). It provides a sound framework where agents can interact with existing software to perform actions in an autonomous way. Agentic AI is the new term to denote these AI-based autonomous systems. In real multi-agent systems, agents need to deal with malicious agents some of which can exploit security vulnerabilities to do harm. A memory poisoning attack is an example of exploiting a vulnerability to modify agents knowledge and, thus, affect its behavior. In an agent, there are different types of memory systems (semantic, episodic, and short-term) which have their own characteristics and for which different memory poisoning attacks may be developed. In this paper we focus on semantic memory, we discuss its attack, and mitigation strategies. We introduce private knowledge retrieval and private inference. We propose a signature system in the knowledge base to prevent from undesired manipulation. This should avoid memory poisoning attacks by introducing security by design in the construction of the semantic memory. In our architecture, an agent contains a local Prolog-like inference system (i.e., using Horn clauses to represent knowledge) which accesses an external knowledge base to get the required knowledge. This externally signed knowledge base is accessed privately. We provide different implementations in Python using different privacy levels including k-anonymity and information-theoretical privacy (IT-PIR).

papers.title: AgenticConflictLens: From Long Traffic Videos to Verifiable Conflict Evidence
papers.abstract: Traffic cameras continuously record urban road-user behavior, providing proactive safety evidence beyond crash reports. Yet safety-critical events - conflicts, near misses, unsafe turns, sudden braking, and crosswalk interactions - are rare and brief, buried in hours of routine footage. Existing traffic-video pipelines extract detections, trajectories, and risk scores but process footage uniformly, without adapting to an analyst's query. Vision-language methods improve scene understanding but often lack traffic-specific verification of participant-level conflicts. We introduce AgenticConflictLens, an agentic, query-conditioned framework for efficient, auditable conflict extraction from long fixed-camera traffic videos. Given a natural-language safety query, a Traffic-Aware Controller combines structured traffic memory with specialized conflict-analysis tools to choose where to search, which road users to examine, and which evidence to verify or reject. A coarse-to-fine search retrieves candidate intervals and applies detailed verification selectively. The framework produces conflict records with refined time intervals, participant pairs, semantic regions, trajectories, motion evidence, uncertainty, rejection reasons, and supporting clips. On 96 annotated hours from Bellevue and NYC DOT, AgenticConflictLens achieves the highest conflict-existence F1 and temporal IoU on both datasets: 0.84 F1/0.77 tIoU on Bellevue and 0.80 F1/0.73 tIoU on NYC DOT, while inspecting only 8.7% and 11.9% of video, respectively. These results support scalable, evidence-grounded urban traffic-safety analysis.

papers.title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
papers.brief: 该框架先用离线深度、手部几何和示范训练动作条件世界模型，再冻结模型并对齐策略查询，将预测性空间知识迁入策略潜变量；部署仅保留策略。
papers.tldr: 将空间动态知识注入灵巧操作策略，无需在线预测即可提升仿真与实机成功率。
papers.what_it_is: 该框架先用离线深度、手部几何和示范训练动作条件世界模型，再冻结模型并对齐策略查询，将预测性空间知识迁入策略潜变量；部署仅保留策略。
key_points: 世界模型预测三维手部点运动与视觉特征变化，覆盖遮挡手指
对齐策略查询与世界查询，部署无需深度或显式未来预测
papers.why_notable: 将训练期的空间预测能力迁入部署策略，避免在线世界模型预测，并在仿真与实机上验证收益，为灵巧操作提供实用的动态知识注入路径。
papers.abstract: Dexterous manipulation requires rich spatial foresight over both the surrounding scene and the robot hand. Existing world-action models often acquire such predictive knowledge through explicit future prediction. We introduce DexForesight, a framework that learns spatial foresight implicitly by injecting dynamics-aware world representations into the latent space of a dexterous policy. During training, DexForesight learns an action-conditioned spatial world model from offline scene depth, kinematic hand geometry, and demonstration trajectories. The world model predicts 3D hand-point motion and visual feature changes, capturing both articulated hand dynamics and scene changes under demonstrated actions, including the motion of fingers occluded from the cameras. We then freeze the world model and align policy queries with its predictive world queries, transferring the learned spatial dynamics into policy latents and using them to condition action generation. At deployment, only the policy is retained, operating on RGB observations, language, and robot state without depth input or explicit future prediction. On 11 DexJoCo simulation tasks, DexForesight improves the overall success rate of the base policy from 49.4% to 60.5%. On three real-robot dexterous manipulation tasks, DexForesight achieves 58.3% success, compared with 50.0% for the strongest baseline. Project page https://dexforesight.github.io/

papers.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
papers.brief: ProTEUS以深度突变扫描数据预训练，用MutationFormer融合序列、进化与结构信息，将变体视为状态、突变视为动作，并通过实验反馈优化目标表型。
papers.tldr: 用突变级世界模型连接虚拟筛选与实验反馈，实现蛋白质闭环进化优化。
papers.what_it_is: ProTEUS以深度突变扫描数据预训练，用MutationFormer融合序列、进化与结构信息，将变体视为状态、突变视为动作，并通过实验反馈优化目标表型。
key_points: MutationFormer采用突变偏置注意力，预测突变功能效应
物理约束全原子预测器比AlphaFold3快逾10倍
两项酶工程闭环实验获得活性超野生型10倍的变体
papers.why_notable: 将突变预测、快速结构评估与实验学习串成闭环，并在两种酶的多目标工程中验证，有望提高有限实验预算下的蛋白质优化效率。
papers.abstract: Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. Thus, a central challenge is to efficiently traverse the large combinatorial space of mutations in silico. We introduce ProTEUS, a mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution. Pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, ProTEUS learns a joint representation of sequence, evolutionary, and structural information using MutationFormer, a mutation-biased attention architecture. Variants are represented as states in this joint latent space, and mutations define actions whose functional consequences are predicted. To support exploration of many mutants, we developed a fast, physics-constrained all-atom predictor that utilizes explicit geometric constraint enforcement to achieve >10 fold increase in speed than AlphaFold3 with guaranteed physical validity. Lastly, ProTEUS refines its prediction and understanding of protein activity through closed loop experimental feedback to guide evolution toward a desired phenotype. ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type. ProTEUS provides a world-model framework that connects virtual evaluation of mutational outcomes with experimental learning for efficient protein evolution.

papers.title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
papers.brief: PhyRubric在观看视频前，按提示词构建语义与物理检查项，再依据带时间戳的证据逐项判定、汇总评分，并配套构建基准、训练开源评判模型。
papers.tldr: 用逐项量规和时间戳证据诊断生成视频的物理常识错误，并训练开源评判模型。
papers.what_it_is: PhyRubric在观看视频前，按提示词构建语义与物理检查项，再依据带时间戳的证据逐项判定、汇总评分，并配套构建基准、训练开源评判模型。
key_points: PhyRubric按提示词预设量规，以时间戳证据支撑逐项判定
基准覆盖5个物理领域、34类；训练集含3,788段视频
评测10个生成模型，开源评判器与人类判断相关性匹敌Gemini 4 Argon
papers.why_notable: 将直觉式总分转为可追溯的物理错误诊断，便于定位生成模型短板；开源评判器也为规模化评测提供了更强工具。
papers.abstract: As text-to-video (T2V) models are increasingly positioned as world simulators, it is essential to evaluate whether their videos conform to physical commonsense. However, existing benchmarks rely on annotators who rate each video with a single score based on intuition, yielding ratings that are subjective and do not tell which physical principle is violated. We introduce PhyRubric, a rubric-grounded diagnostic framework for evaluating physical commonsense in T2V generation. For each caption, PhyRubric constructs a caption-specific rubric before any video is seen, decomposing the caption into semantic and physical items, and derives scores from item-level verdicts grounded in timestamped evidence. We instantiate this framework as PhyRubric-Bench, which spans 34 categories across five physical domains, and scale it up to PhyRubric-Train with 3,788 videos, on which we fine-tune the open-source PhyRubric-Judge. Empirical results across ten T2V models show that physical commonsense remains far from solved, and that PhyRubric-Judge correlates more closely with human judgments than existing open-source judges while matching the frontier proprietary Gemini 4 Argon. Further analysis provides actionable insights for T2V models.

papers.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
papers.brief: TorchCurves是一个PyTorch库，用B样条或Legendre多项式表示向量值曲线，将批量标量映射为曲线点，并支持输入与系数的梯度传播。
papers.tldr: 将参数曲线变为可学习模块，支持输入与系数求导并融入神经网络。
papers.what_it_is: TorchCurves是一个PyTorch库，用B样条或Legendre多项式表示向量值曲线，将批量标量映射为曲线点，并支持输入与系数的梯度传播。
key_points: 曲线系数可联合训练，也可由另一网络生成
提供可训练模块、基函数模块及函数式接口
对比NumPy、SciPy求值及EfficientKAN训练
papers.why_notable: 为连续特征嵌入、KAN和函数回归提供可复用的曲线组件；性能实验也揭示了通用实现的实用范围与开销。
papers.abstract: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes. The results illustrate where this generality remains computationally practical and where overhead is substantial. Library is available on GitHub at https://github.com/alexshtf/torchcurves.

papers.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
papers.brief: 研究用暂停、手腕微动和时间戳缩放，诊断记忆增强VLA的虚假进度现象。结果表明，按时间采样的记忆诱发捷径，改用事件索引可无需重训缓解。
papers.tldr: 记忆增强机器人策略会把时间流逝误当任务进度，按事件索引可缓解误判。
papers.what_it_is: 研究用暂停、手腕微动和时间戳缩放，诊断记忆增强VLA的虚假进度现象。结果表明，按时间采样的记忆诱发捷径，改用事件索引可无需重训缓解。
key_points: RoboMME两项任务成功数从47、44降至16、10，均为50次试验
仅缩放时间戳即可诱发提前停止或重复，移除时间编码仍无效
事件索引无需重训挽回至少一半损失；暂停增强训练反而损害计数
papers.why_notable: 揭示机器人记忆可能学到时钟而非事件，且漏洞不只来自时间编码；为长程任务中的记忆设计提供了直接、低成本的修正方向。
papers.abstract: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. Because time passes even when nothing happens, such a memory may not tell waiting from working. We show that it does not. On the counting tasks of RoboMME, we make the robot briefly pause or fidget its wrist. Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early. We call this failure phantom progress. It cuts success from 47 to 16 of 50 on one task and from 44 to 10 on the other. When the same frames are withheld from memory, success returns, so the cause lies in memory rather than in the interruption itself. We trace the failure to a temporal shortcut: because demonstrations proceed at a steady pace, elapsed time predicts progress. Indeed, rescaling the time stamps alone makes the policy stop early when the clock runs fast and repeat when it runs slow. Surprisingly, removing the time encoding does not cure the failure, because the frames of a null event still occupy slots of the time-sampled memory. Across RoboMME's released designs, vulnerability follows how memory is indexed. Of the fixes the diagnosis suggests, training with injected pauses does not remove the failure and impairs counting, whereas indexing memory by events recovers half or more of the loss without retraining. A memory meant to remember what happened should count events rather than clock ticks.

papers.title: From Tool State to Scientific Action: Auditing Decision Provenance in Biomedical Research Agents
papers.brief: BioAgent-DF在同一科学计算位置配对保存参考值与候选值，通过原位恢复或移植后重跑智能体，追踪数值状态、证据引用和实验决策之间的因果联系。
papers.tldr: 通过状态恢复与移植审计科研智能体，揭示结论不变也可能掩盖证据与行动偏移。
papers.what_it_is: BioAgent-DF在同一科学计算位置配对保存参考值与候选值，通过原位恢复或移植后重跑智能体，追踪数值状态、证据引用和实验决策之间的因果联系。
key_points: 8批SciFact测试中，7组配置反复出现证据变化
hERG任务恢复执行状态与认证分数，纠正39项决策
流式算术校验较原FP64实现节省42.4%总时间
papers.why_notable: 将科研智能体审计从最终答案扩展到证据和行动链，说明仅替换预测文件不足以修复已受污染的决策过程，并展示可验证的恢复路径。
papers.abstract: A scientific agent can give the same verdict while reading and citing different evidence. BioAgent-DF tests this separation using paired reference and candidate values saved at the same scientific computation site. It restores or transplants those values at their original coordinates, then runs the agent on healthy hardware. Across eight SciFact batches, Qwen3.5-4B shows repeatable citation changes in three capture-claim combinations, and Gemma 3 4B IT shows repeatable read and citation changes in four. These seven combinations cover two claims. Full restoration recovers the reference evidence sets while verdicts remain unchanged. Verdict changes observed under the baseline prompt did not recur under the explicit-example prompt. Complementary tool and optimizer experiments distinguish recovery of numerical state, recovery of ranked lists, and restoration of an agent's visible history. These results show that an audit should track both the evidence an agent uses and its final answer. In hERG cardiac-safety assay allocation, silent numerical faults changed testing decisions while the fixed-budget shortlist kept the same number of compounds labeled as blockers. After the agent had used faulty values, restoring its earlier execution state and supplying certified scores recovered all 39 changed decisions, whereas replacing the prediction file recovered none; no incorrect action was committed. A streaming implementation of the arithmetic checks reduced the total time for forward execution and verification by 42.4% relative to the original FP64 implementation, with identical flags and recovery outputs.

papers.title: Market-Conditioned JEPA: Learning from Unpredictable Market Shocks
papers.brief: MC-JEPA用其他资产的未来目标嵌入构造留一市场条件，再通过自身表征生成的因子载荷融入预测，使模型同时学习市场暴露与资产特有成分。
papers.tldr: 借助训练期已实现的市场冲击，改善金融自监督表征与风险、流动性预测。
papers.what_it_is: MC-JEPA用其他资产的未来目标嵌入构造留一市场条件，再通过自身表征生成的因子载荷融入预测，使模型同时学习市场暴露与资产特有成分。
key_points: 潜在因子模型证明：市场条件降低特有成分学习噪声
11年分钟级A股数据，覆盖收益、暴露等9类目标
所有流动性及2小时至5天收益目标的RankIC最优
papers.why_notable: 将不可预测的市场冲击转化为训练信号，在风险与流动性任务上收益尤为显著；无需标签也能学出接近监督探针的市场贝塔排序。
papers.abstract: Much of the variation in financial time series is driven by market-wide shocks that cannot be predicted from an asset's own history. Per-asset self-supervised learning treats this variation as irreducible noise. Under a latent factor model, we show that conditioning prediction on the realized market factor makes the asset's market exposure necessary for optimal prediction, while reducing the noise against which the asset-specific component is learned. Building on this insight, we introduce Market-Conditioned JEPA (MC-JEPA), a joint-embedding predictive architecture for financial time series. During training, we construct a leave-one-out market condition for each asset from the future target embeddings of other assets and incorporate it through factor loadings derived from the asset's own representation. On 11 years of minute-level Chinese A-share data, MC-JEPA improves over per-asset JEPA across nine targets spanning returns, market exposure, risk, and liquidity, with the strongest and most statistically significant gains in exposure, risk, and liquidity. It achieves the best RankIC on all liquidity targets and on return horizons from two hours to five days, outperforming time-series foundation models and self-supervised baselines, and delivers the best portfolio performance in a historical backtest. Ablations show that the return and exposure gains require the condition to be aligned with the realized market movement. After restoring the volatility scale removed by normalization, the predictor's factor loadings rank stocks by market beta nearly as well as a supervised probe, without labels. A synthetic factor-model study with known parameters shows that conditioning improves the recovery of both market exposure and the asset-specific component.

papers.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
papers.brief: Sable证明已承诺的量化模型确实由指定提示生成给定序列。它将推理定义为无浮点的确定性整数函数，结合小域sumcheck与张量承诺，逐层流式生成证明。
papers.tldr: 将大模型推理转为确定性整数计算，用单卡生成逐比特正确性证明。
papers.what_it_is: Sable证明已承诺的量化模型确实由指定提示生成给定序列。它将推理定义为无浮点的确定性整数函数，结合小域sumcheck与张量承诺，逐层流式生成证明。
key_points: 合并zerocheck与LogUp-GKR，每域一次sumcheck
单卡证明Qwen2.5-32B的4096词元耗时92.5秒
证明耗时为推理的41至50倍，且不具零知识性
papers.why_notable: 把数百亿参数模型的可验证推理推进到单卡分钟级，较zkLLM显著提速；但整数版本并非原始BF16模型的完全等价替代。
papers.abstract: We present Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover for the statement that a committed, integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a given prompt, bit for bit. Sable fixes an integer function F_O with no floating-point step, in which every rounding, normalization, softmax and sampling decision is determined by its inputs, and proves it with a constraint system whose relations provably never wrap modulo the 31-bit KoalaBear prime. The proof batches zerochecks and LogUp-GKR lookups into one sumcheck per domain, and commits to every witness tensor and weight in one multilinear commitment built from Reed-Solomon codes, BLAKE3 Merkle trees and a mixed-length BaseFold opening. The prover streams the model layer by layer on one GPU. On one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, Sable proves all 64 layers of Qwen2.5-32B in 92.5 s for 4,096 tokens and 398 s for 16,384 tokens, and covers Qwen3-32B and the mixture-of-experts Qwen3-30B-A3B (4,096 tokens in 121.8 and 84.7 s). A proof costs 41 to 50 times the serving time, or 6.4 cents per 4,096-token request at public GPU prices, and 40 to 64 times less time per parameter and token than zkLLM. On WikiText-2, F_O's greedy token matches the BF16 model's at 86.3% of positions; on Qwen3, F_O is within 1.6 points of BF16 on MMLU and 1.7 points on GSM8K. A verifier with a compiled core checks a proof on one CPU core in 19 to 56 s. In the random-oracle model, the interactive proof has round-by-round soundness error 2^-103. The proof is not zero-knowledge, so the system targets open-weight models. Code: https://github.com/moonmath-ai/Sable

papers.title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control
papers.brief: ExRL为基础策略增添轻量适配器，用离策略强化学习预测每个动作块执行多久。它不直接优化高维动作序列，而是在低维执行时长空间中完成在线适配。
papers.tldr: 通过学习动作块执行时长，降低机器人长动作块策略在线适配的数据成本。
papers.what_it_is: ExRL为基础策略增添轻量适配器，用离策略强化学习预测每个动作块执行多久。它不直接优化高维动作序列，而是在低维执行时长空间中完成在线适配。
key_points: ExRL将优化目标从动作序列改为执行长度
轻量适配器通过离策略强化学习训练
仿真与真实机器人任务验证多类长动作块策略
papers.why_notable: 它把长动作块的在线适配转化为低维控制问题，在交互数据昂贵的机器人任务中提高样本效率，并减少任务专属调参。
papers.abstract: Predicting long action chunks, often spanning dozens of timesteps, has become a key ingredient in increasingly capable robot policies. In this paper, we find that adapting these long-chunk policies with existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods can require many online samples due to the high dimensionality of the action chunks being optimized, making such adaptation impractical in real-world scenarios where interaction data are costly to collect. Our key insight is to shift adaptation from optimizing actions to optimizing how long to execute each predicted action chunk. This keeps the adaptation space low-dimensional while its expressivity grows with the chunk size. We thus introduce Execution at the Right Length (ExRL), a simple approach which augments the base policy with a lightweight adapter that predicts the execution length of each chunk and is trained using off-policy RL algorithms. Across simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks, ExRL enables sample-efficient adaptation of a diverse range of long-chunk policies with minimal task-specific hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: Are Causal Neuron Circuits Unique and Transferable?
papers.brief: 研究神经元干预是否必要、唯一且可迁移。对每组选定的12个MLP神经元穷举4096个子集，通过清零和激活替换，比较答案变化与跨输入效果。
papers.tldr: 穷举神经元子集发现，改写答案的因果干预常有多种替代组合，跨题迁移有限。
papers.what_it_is: 研究神经元干预是否必要、唯一且可迁移。对每组选定的12个MLP神经元穷举4096个子集，通过清零和激活替换，比较答案变化与跨输入效果。
key_points: 首都任务清零12个神经元使答案边际降27%，跨题激活替换几乎无效
两跳激活替换：Qwen与Llama均9/11条链转向桥接实体
4096子集穷举显示少量或不相交子集可独立翻转答案
papers.why_notable: 将“干预有效”与“承载题目内容、必要且唯一”区分开来，为因果可解释性提供更严格的检验，并揭示同题改写之外的迁移局限。
papers.abstract: Interpretability demonstrations often show that intervening on a group of neurons changes a model's answer. A recent example removes an 18-neuron group in Qwen3-32B and the model answers "Simba" instead of "Scar" to a two-hop Lion King riddle. Such a demonstration establishes that the group matters, but not how much of it is necessary, whether other groups could do the same, or whether the effect carries over to other inputs. We ask: when intervening on a group of neurons changes a model's answer, how much of that group is actually necessary? For every selected group we measure all 4,096 subsets of 12 MLP neurons.
